title: Catégorie des types de mots [dont arbres plans] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck uses the purely combinatorial notion of a map (carte). A map is a set A of oriented edges (half-edges, i.e. darts). It carries a fixed-point-free involution σ, which reverses orientation, and a permutation ρ, the rotation of darts around each vertex. The faces are then the cycles of ρσ, or of σρ depending on convention. The pages are dated 1982 or later, so they come just before the Esquisse d'un programme (1984).

The contour. A 'contour' C is a combinatorial oriented polygon. It consists of a cyclically ordered set A(C) of edges, with its 'fundamental rotation' ρ_C, a single cycle. On top of this it carries a fixed-point-free involution σ_C on A(C), that is, a pairing of the sides.

The main claim. From (C, ρ_C, σ_C) one recovers a 'circular graph' Γ, which is a connected map with a single face (a unicellular map). The dictionary is:
- A(Γ) ≅ A(C);
- σ_Γ = σ_C;
- ρ_Γσ_Γ = ρ_C (the face permutation of Γ is the contour rotation);
- hence ρ_Γ = ρ_Cσ_C.
The last two lines are consistent, since ρ_Γ = ρ_C σ_C^{-1} = ρ_C σ_C. Grothendieck phrases this as an equivalence of categories: unicellular maps on one side, oriented contours with a fixed-point-free involution on the other.

Geometric picture (spelled out on the next page). The surface |Γ| is obtained from the disc bounded by C by gluing side a to side σ_C a with reversed orientation. This is the classical description of a one-face map as a pairwise side-gluing of a 2n-gon.

Boxed statement. Γ is a tree if and only if two conditions hold:
- C is a genuine (non-degenerate) polygon;
- σ_C is totally non-crossing: for any two disjoint σ_C-orbits {a, σa} and {b, σb}, the pairs do not interleave in the cyclic order.
This is the genus-0 case of the gluing picture. Plane trees correspond to non-crossing perfect matchings of the 2n sides, i.e. to the contour walk / Dyck word of the tree. This links back to the folder's theme, 'types de mots' (types of words), including plane trees.

The next page confirms the reading. Trees are realised by drawing non-crossing chords between the midpoints of paired sides in the disc. Regions then become vertices, and the common boundaries of regions become edges.
errors: No mathematical error. Correctness of the box: a one-face map with n edges and V vertices has genus g = (n+1-V)/2, so it is a tree iff g = 0 iff V = n+1. It is standard that this happens exactly when the side-pairing of the 2n-gon is non-crossing.

The degenerate case needs care. The one-vertex tree with no edges has an empty contour; 'non ponctuel' (not reduced to a point) presumably means C has at least one side. Plane trees 'in a plane not necessarily oriented' (next page) also require a treatment of reflection, which is only sketched.

ideas.what: Encoding a connected map by a dart set with an involution σ and a rotation ρ; faces given by ρσ
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial maps / rotation systems (permutation encoding of maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heffter, Edmonds (1960), Tutte, A. Jacques (1968–70), Cori (1975)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2–3 (cartes via the cartographic group)

ideas.what: Equivalence between one-face maps and polygons whose sides are paired by a fixed-point-free involution, with ρ_Γ = ρ_Cσ_C, σ_Γ = σ_C
ideas.modern_name: Unicellular maps ↔ gluings of a 2n-gon (side pairings)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical surface topology; enumerated by Walsh–Lehman (1972), Harer–Zagier (1986)

ideas.what: Γ is a tree iff the side-pairing of its contour polygon is non-crossing
ideas.modern_name: Plane trees ↔ non-crossing perfect matchings (contour walk / Dyck words, Catalan numbers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical folklore of enumerative combinatorics (Catalan objects)

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but classical reformulation: one-face maps as polygon side-pairings, with trees corresponding to non-crossing pairings. All of this was known in map enumeration by the early 1970s. The categorical phrasing and the link to 'types of words' fit Grothendieck's dessins-d'enfants period, but they add nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The second line of the correspondence table should almost certainly read σ_Γ ⟷ σ_C, not σ_Γ ⟷ ρ_C. This is consistent with the earlier equation σ_Γ = σ_C and with the line ρ_Γ = ρ_Cσ_C.
The third line is ρ_Γσ_Γ ⟵ ρ_C (the transcription shows a corrected 'ρ_Γ^σ').
'graphes combinatoires circulaires Γ (cartes ...)': the parenthetical seems to describe one-face maps rather than 'cartes connexes notés'. It is illegible; read with caution.
The left margin note is very uncertain. It probably comments on the relation to the usual definition of plane graphs, and says that ρ_Γ is the natural rotation for the map attached to Γ.
The end of the box probably reads: 'pour deux orbites disjointes d'arêtes sous σ_C, [les paires] ne se croisent pas' (non-crossing). The garbled 'compositions et n.p.' should be read this way.
